entry.title: I couldn't say in one sentence what to tell users when we used AI. So I built a drafter.
entry.summary: We shipped a feature that used a model to summarize support tickets. Quietly. And then a reviewer asked the only question that mattered: when a user reads the output, are we telling them it was generated by AI? I didn't have an answer, and the EU AI Act expects one. Articles 49 and 50 of the Act are about exactly this — telling people when AI is involved, whether that's a general-purpose model's capabilities or AI-generated content a user might mistake for human-made. The obligation is concrete wording, aimed at the user, at the point of interaction. I kept getting it wrong because "disclose that AI was used" is a sentence, not a disclosure. The duty isn't "mention AI somewhere." It's specific: what was used, that the output was AI-generated or manipulated, and enough that a person can mak…

entry.title: Replacing Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms when I move a client site from WordPress to Astro
entry.summary:
Every WordPress site I migrate to Astro has the same hidden landmine. It's not the theme, it's not the blog posts. It's the forms. Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, WPForms, sometimes all three on one site because three different devs touched it over the years. The client doesn't think about any of it. They just know leads show up in their inbox. If that stops the day you launch, you hear about it in about two weeks when they ask why the phone went quiet. So here's the checklist I run now before I touch DNS. I don't trust the menu. I search the database export for shortcodes and blocks: grep -oE '\[(contact-form-7|gravityform|wpforms)[^]]*\]' wp-export.xml | sort | uniq -c grep -o 'wp:gravityforms/form[^>]*' wp-export.xml | sort | uniq -c

entry.summary: Agent-driven data pipelines break when upstream APIs change field types, add nested objects, or return inconsistent structures. entry.title: How AIClaw 3.7.32 Routes Models by Service Contract
entry.summary: A model's original vendor does not tell a desktop agent which HTTP interface to call. A gateway can serve models from several vendors through one contract, while a direct connection may need a different protocol for a particular model. Putting the protocol choice on every model makes a large catalog tedious to configure. Guessing from a model name can also send the right model to the wrong interface. AIClaw 3.7.32 introduces service-aware routing: resolve the connection contract first, apply scoped model rules where they are known, and keep manual exceptions in advanced settings. This is in the published release, rather than an unreleased proposal. All implementation links below are pinned to that tag.
